title: Lime boosts scooter availability in existing cities, says CEO
excerpt: Lime CEO Wayne Ting focuses on adding scooters and bicycles in US cities to enhance reliability and rider engagement after company's IPO.
content_html:
Lime is doubling down on cities where it already operates. It's about creating more loyal riders, its CEO says

By Alex Bitter

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Expect to see even more Lime scooters and bikes zooming around major US cities.

Wayne Ting, Lime's CEO, told Business Insider on Tuesday that the company is focused on getting more of its vehicles on the roads where it already operates rather than making a big push to expand to more cities.

Ting made the comments on the same day that Lime reported quarterly earnings results for the first time. Revenue grew 24% to $304 million for the second quarter, and the company posted net income of $295 million, including the benefits of its IPO in July.

Shares of Lime rose about 2% in after-hours trading.

Getting riders to use Lime more frequently will be key to making the company consistently profitable, Ting said.

Lime operates in about 60 US cities. By adding more vehicles to its existing fleets, Ting said, Lime makes it easier for users to find a ride near them.

That's particularly important as Lime grows its paid subscription options, such as LimePass, which offers a discount on the company's usual per-minute rate if riders buy ahead of time.

"You're going to continue to see us invest in our existing markets to grow reliability," he said. "And, by growing reliability, we can also engage our riders more frequently."

Lime's monthly active users grew 22% during its second quarter, topping 5 million for the first time.

Ting said that Lime is "an AI-resilient business," because it sells real-world rides on scooters and bikes. "There's no amount of vibe-coding that is going to get you physical transportation," he said.

Even so, Lime is using AI in its operations, he said.

The company uses a machine-learning algorithm to determine where to position scooters and bikes in each city based on demand, Ting said. The tech allows the company to "optimize revenue or profits," he added.

There's also a benefit for riders, Ting said: They're more likely to find a scooter or bike nearby when they need one.

"Reliability is both the number of bikes and scooters you have, but it's also making sure they're at the right place at the right time," he said.

content_html_zh:
Lime正在加倍投入其已经运营的城市。 其首席执行官表示，这是为了创造更多忠诚的骑手

作者：Alex Bitter 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

预计将会看到更多 Lime 踏板车和自行车在美国主要城市中驰骋。

Lime 首席执行官韦恩·丁 (Wayne Ting) 周二向《商业内幕》表示，该公司的重点是让更多车辆在已运营的道路上行驶，而不是大力推动向更多城市扩张。

丁在 Lime 首次报告季度盈利结果的同一天发表了上述言论。 第二季度收入增长 24%，达到 3.04 亿美元，净利润为 2.95 亿美元，其中包括 7 月份 IPO 带来的收益。

Lime 股价在盘后交易中上涨约 2%。

Ting 表示，让乘客更频繁地使用 Lime 将是公司持续盈利的关键。

Lime 在美国约 60 个城市开展业务。 Ting 表示，通过向现有车队添加更多车辆，Lime 可以让用户更轻松地找到附近的乘车服务。

随着 Lime 不断增加其付费订阅选项（例如 LimePass），这一点尤其重要。如果乘客提前购买，LimePass 会比公司通常的每分钟费率提供折扣。

“你将继续看到我们对现有市场进行投资以提高可靠性，”他说。 “而且，通过提高可靠性，我们还可以更频繁地吸引乘客。”

Lime 的月活跃用户在第二季度增长了 22%，首次突破 500 万。

Ting 表示，Lime 是“一家具有人工智能弹性的企业”，因为它销售现实世界中的踏板车和自行车。 “再多的振动编码也无法让你获得物理交通，”他说。

即便如此，Lime 仍在运营中使用人工智能，他说。

丁说，该公司使用机器学习算法来根据需求确定每个城市的踏板车和自行车的放置位置。 他补充说，这项技术使公司能够“优化收入或利润”。

丁说，这对骑手来说还有一个好处：当他们需要时，他们更有可能在附近找到一辆踏板车或自行车。

“可靠性既是指你拥有的自行车和踏板车的数量，也是确保它们在正确的时间出现在正确的地点，”他说。

亚历克斯·比特（Alex Bitter）是一位资深零售记者，报道零工经济、食品和零售业。 他的工作重点是主要的零工配送和叫车应用程序，包括 Uber、Lyft、DoorDash、Instacart 和沃尔玛的 Spark。 他对从应用程序上工作的感觉到公司的业务战略等一切都很感兴趣。他最近的一些故事讲述了在应用程序上被停用的零工工人、DoorDash 雇用传统员工进行送货、零工工人使用机器人以及零工工作扩展到护理等新职业。亚历克斯还撰写了有关阿尔迪在美国的扩张、星巴克的扭亏为盈以及卡夫亨氏预算削减的影响的文章。 便利店连锁店 Sheetz 在他的报道后结束了“微笑政策”。在 2020 年 9 月加入 Insider 之前，他为标准普尔全球市场情报撰写了有关消费者和零售公司的文章。 他毕业于夏威夷大学马诺阿分校，在大岛长大。亚历克斯住在华盛顿特区，你可以发现他在空闲时间研究古钱币或用金属探测器寻找内战文物。有提示吗？ 请通过 abitter@businessinsider.com 或通过加密消息应用程序 Signal 联系，电话 +1 (808) 854-4501。
